articles.content_orig:
‘The Big Money Show’ panel sounds off on Jerome Powell’s decision to stay at the Federal Reserve, as tensions rise with President Donald Trump and incoming Chair Kevin Warsh over interest rate policy.
The inspector general's investigation into the Federal Reserve's costly renovation project determined that there was no administrative misconduct after the cost overruns prompted an investigation of former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid criticism from President Donald Trump.
The Office of Inspector General for the Federal Reserve's Board of Governors began investigating the cost overruns at Powell's request in July 2025. Powell, then the Fed chair, disclosed in January that the Department of Justice opened a criminal probe into his June 2025 testimony before Congress about the renovation project. The U.S. Attorney's Office closed the investigation in April as the inspector general continued its probe into the matter.
"At no point during our evaluation did we find reasonable grounds to believe that a violation of federal criminal law had occurred requiring a referral to the U.S. Attorney General in accordance with the Inspector General Act," the IG report states.
"Further, while our report outlines deficiencies in the management of the renovation project, resulting in our recommended corrective actions in accordance with the Inspector General Act, we did not identify administrative misconduct during our evaluation," the report added.
POWELL SAYS HE'LL STAY ON FED BOARD AFTER CHAIRMANSHIP ENDS BUT WON'T BE A 'SHADOW FED CHAIR'
The inspector general found no administrative misconduct in the management of the Federal Reserve's renovation project after then-Fed Chair Jerome Powell was criticized by President Donald Trump. (Kent Nishimura/Reuters)
President Donald Trump repeatedly criticized Powell over the project last year, accusing him of "gross incompetence" and threatening to sue the Fed leader at the time. The president also said he was considering firing Powell over the project and urged him to resign, while also calling on the central bank to cut interest rates.
In January, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro issued subpoenas to the Fed's Board of Governors regarding Powell's testimony on the project.
Powell responded by releasing a video statement saying that the "unprecedented" move was politically motivated, arguing that the "threat of criminal charges is a consequence of the Federal Reserve setting interest rates based on our best assessment of what will serve the public, rather than following the preferences of the President."
POWELL ASKS FOR IG REVIEW AFTER TRUMP ADMINISTRATION FLAGS FED'S COSTLY BUILDING RENOVATION
The the Marriner S. Eccles Federal Reserve building serves as the central bank's headquarters. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The controversial project involved the renovation of the Fed's Marriner S. Eccles and 1951 Constitution Avenue NW buildings. The approved budget grew from $1.317 billion in February 2020 to $2.381 billion in December 2024, which the IG noted was the Fed board's most recently revised renovation budget. The Fed board also received a proposed construction cost of $2.135 billion from its construction manager in January.
Critics of the project took issue with a number of design elements in the renovation project, such as the inclusion of a garden terrace, marble and water features. However, the IG "determined that these features did not materially contribute to subsequent construction cost increases."
The Fed attributed some of the cost increases to higher costs of construction materials, equipment and labor; changes to original designs after consulting with review agencies; and unforeseen issues like more asbestos than anticipated, contaminated soil, and a higher-than-expected water table.
Trump and Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., made a highly-publicized visit to the construction site with Powell last summer. (Andrew Caballero-Reynolds/AFP)
The IG's report acknowledged that those issues all contributed to the overall cost increases, but emphasized that project management and contract execution decisions also played a role. Among those decisions were not establishing a guaranteed maximum price contract that would make the contractor responsible for cost overruns.
Additionally, the IG noted that substantial cost increases were caused by four price packages, of which three didn't receive at least three bids, and said the Fed didn't effectively use its outside construction representative or have sufficient internal project governance. It also noted the construction phase of the project is expected to end by December 2027.
FORMER FED CHAIR JEROME POWELL SELLS MARYLAND WATERFRONT ESTATE FOR $7.2M: REPORT
Trump nominated Powell as Fed chair during his first term as president. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)
President Trump responded to the IG report in a post on his Truth Social platform, saying that "'Too Late' Powell should be forced to resign from the Board. He can't manage a Building, and he certainly shouldn't be allowed to manage his High Interest Rate Policy (only on ‘TRUMP!’)."
"I have asked Attorney General Todd Blanche to study the report, and make a determination as to what to do about relatively small Building Complex that is Hundreds of Millions of Dollars over budget, and is now going to cost, according to the Report, at least 2.5 Billion Dollars, with no end in sight," Trump continued, criticizing the management of the project.
"I could have done a far better Renovation for 25 Million Dollars, completely maintaining the MAGNIFICENCE of the structure, and had money left over," Trump claimed. "They completely destroyed the Beauty and Glorious History of the Building."
"This is Jerome Powell's fault, and he should be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY! If he doesn't resign, he should be sued, at the highest level, by the United States Government, for either corruption or incompetence, both of which are completely unacceptable…And no, I do not want this building named after President Donald J. Trump, ME! Thank you for your attention to this matter," the president wrote.
GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh succeeded Powell in May after his nomination was allowed to advance following the DOJ's decision to drop its investigation into Powell, which prompted resistance to Warsh's nomination in the Senate.
Powell remains a member of the Fed's Board of Governors after signaling he would stay on until the investigation into him was over with finality due to his concerns about threats to the independence of monetary policy.
The Warsh-led Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously earlier this month to raise interest rates for the first time since 2023 due to stubborn inflation.

Morning Rundown: Victim’s mother describes failed execution, Flydubai pilot hailed a hero, and Cornell student’s police statement reveals new details
The Cornell University student who alleged in a lawsuit that she was gang-raped and plied with drugs at a fraternity house in 2024 described the hourslong incident to police in a sworn statement, according to the document, which was obtained by NBC News.
Jane Doe told police in part that she had agreed to an initial sexual encounter with two of the men, described being encouraged to take drugs and said she did not remember some parts of the night.
“I would say that it was the most intoxicated I’ve ever been in my life,” she told police about how she was feeling later in the evening. “I felt like I was unable to make any decisions because of how intoxicated I was.”
Jane Doe voluntarily gave the sworn statement to Cornell University police on Nov. 14, 2024, 26 days after the alleged assault. In it, she detailed the night of Oct. 19 to 20, when she initially agreed to a threesome, but she said that she felt increasingly incapacitated as the night went on, that she had gaps in her memory and that at one point she was “extremely uncomfortable.”
“Adding to my feelings of isolation was the fact that my phone was across the room and I felt like I couldn’t get to it, as well as I didn’t have any form of payment to order an Uber to get out of the situation I was in,” she told police.
The former student’s lawsuit , filed Sept. 16, has sparked national furor over the university’s and the district attorney’s handling of the case. It has prompted the DA to take a fresh look after his office previously determined there was “insufficient evidence to support criminal charges” when the case was reviewed in 2024.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten released a lengthy statement Monday, which included parts of Doe’s sworn statement to Cornell police in November 2024, and defended his initial decision not to pursue criminal charges.
His statement did not include details in which Doe referred to how, at one point, she felt the most incapacitated she had ever felt in her life, nor how she felt she could not leave the room.
The lawsuit alleges she was sexually assaulted, raped and pressured to snort ketamine after a night of heavy drinking. Her complaint names seven Chi Phi fraternity brothers who she claims sexually assaulted her.
Her statement to police mirrored many of the allegations in the lawsuit. She described drinking sometime after 6:30 p.m., going to two different Ithaca bars and finally going to the Chi Phi fraternity house around 10:30 or 11 p.m. to meet a friend.
There, a friend asked whether she was interested in a threesome, which she said she agreed to.
Later, another man knocked on the door of the room they were in, and she let him in because, she said, she was told it was probably the man whose room they were in. She engaged in a sexual encounter with the third man, the statement said.
“I don’t remember much of this threesome,” she told police. “I was pretty incapacitated.”
While Doe did not remember having sex with the third man, she recalled hearing two men “say something about ‘having a turn.’” That, she told police, made her realize the men were “using me without caring about what I was getting out of the situation.”
At one point, “multiple men walked into the room,” and, she told police, “I was instantly horrified.” She ran across the room to hide under the covers of another bed, the statement said, which she said felt like the only option because they were standing between her and the exit.
The lawsuit says multiple other men entered the room after one fraternity member sent a message to a group chat, a screenshot of which was included in the suit, that said there was “free p----” available upstairs where Doe was.
Doe described her level of intoxication after four more men entered the room and said the night “really becomes a blur for me at that point.”
After one of the men started to kiss her, she told police, she quickly backed away, and she described feeling dissociation.
“I was starting to become completely numb to the whole situation,” she said in the statement.
She said she had taken ketamine earlier in the evening and was offered it again. Doe had never taken the drug before, according to the lawsuit. Her thought, she told police, was that “if I do Ketamine again maybe I will pass out. My thought was that if I passed out and these men had sex with me, then they could be charged with Rape.”
Doe described realizing the next day that what happened to her the previous evening was being talked about on campus. “It was made clear to me by several friends that the members of Chi Phi were bragging,” she told police. She added that “it was now obvious that everyone knew it was me that this had happened to.”
In her statement, she stressed instances of turning men down repeatedly, expressing discomfort and feeling coerced.
Doe also spoke about an alleged encounter after she was ushered upstairs to what she believed was the fraternity president’s office, where, she said, two men “were asking me to have sex so many times that I finally gave in.”
“To me, that felt like coercion,” she said. “Also, I felt like due to my intoxication, they should have known how intoxicated I was based on how I was slurring my words.”
In a transcript of her interview with campus police on Nov. 14, Doe is also alleged to have said, “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped,” CBS News reported Wednesday. NBC News has not seen the full transcript of that interview.
Van Houten told NBC News on Wednesday that the specific allegation was not in the written statement his office received from Cornell police in November 2024 when they were assessing whether or not to bring charges. Cornell has said its campus police department “shared all investigatory information” with the DA’s office.
Van Houten said in his statement Monday that Doe did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped in her sworn statement to police.
“On the contrary, Jane Doe’s statement described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as voluntary, conscious, and consensual,” his statement said.
He also noted that she wrote about having difficulty remembering parts of the night as the evening went on.
Doe’s statement, he said, did not meet the legal bar of proof beyond a reasonable doubt that there was lack of consent under New York State Penal Law . He added that her statement did not allege that she was incapable of controlling her conduct, that drugs were administered without her consent, that she was unconscious or that she did not clearly express that she did not consent.
Van Houten said “multiple prosecutors and criminal investigators reviewed Jane Doe’s statement and correctly determined the alleged facts as set forth in the statement do not constitute a crime.”
“According to the statement, each time Jane Doe asked to stop the sexual conduct, the sexual conduct stopped,” he said.
Doe’s attorney, Thomas P. Giuffra, said he was “very disappointed” in Van Houten’s claim Monday that Doe’s interactions that night were consensual.
“If my client consented, why did you make a complaint to the police and say I’ve been assaulted? Why would she say that a crime occurred? Why would she go to the police in the first place? It makes no sense,” he told NBC News in an interview Monday.
He said in an email Monday that his client was never contacted by the DA’s office nor any investigator other than the officer who took her original complaint, and he called the decision to reconsider prosecution “a step in the right direction, albeit a late one.”

articles.title_orig: Musk returns to Trump world for Pentagon war study
articles.title_zh: Musk returns to Trump world for Pentagon war study
articles.content_orig:
The Pentagon is tapping Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , defense technology entrepreneur and Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey and former House Speaker Newt Gingrich to identify the military capabilities, technologies and weapons the U.S. may need in future wars, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Wednesday.
The initiative, dubbed Project Meridian, will spend 120 days looking years and decades ahead at how warfare could change and what capabilities the U.S. military will need to maintain a technological edge.
"Project Meridian, the future of warfare, is not about developing new strategies or new policies," Hegseth said. Instead, he said, its purpose is to "identify the domains that we must conquer, and capabilities we must master."
Hegseth said the effort will focus on “discovering, developing, and fielding” weapons and systems that future U.S. troops may need on battlefields ranging “from under the Earth to beyond the moon.” He announced the initiative during a "State of the Force" address to junior officers and enlisted leaders at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia.
Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael will oversee the project, with Musk, Luckey and Gingrich as co-leads and a broader team drawn from government, industry, academia and the policy world, Hegseth said.
None of the three co-leads has served in the U.S. military. Musk moved to Canada as a teenager in part, he has said , to avoid compulsory military service in South Africa.
The role puts Musk and Luckey in prime position to help identify the military’s future technology needs while their companies compete for billions in DOD business.
Musk's SpaceX holds a plethora of Pentagon contracts. In May, the Space Force awarded the company a $4.16 billion contract to build satellites designed to track and target airborne threats, just days after awarding SpaceX another $2.29 billion contract for a military satellite communications network.
Luckey's Anduril develops autonomous weapons and other military technology. The Marine Corps awarded the company a contract worth up to $642 million in 2025 for counter-drone systems.
The announcement was part of a broader Pentagon push into autonomous warfare including plans announced Wednesday for a new four-star Autonomous Warfare Command aimed at scaling autonomous and robotic systems across the military.
Anduril, SpaceX, Tesla and Gingrich did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Tennessee governor halts executions after Christa Gail Pike survives lethal injection
articles.title_zh: Tennessee governor halts executions after Christa Gail Pike survives lethal injection
articles.content_orig:
Emergency vehicles arrive at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution after the execution of Christa Pike was halted Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. George Walker IV/AP hide caption
NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Tennessee officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death Wednesday for a 1995 murder after administering two doses of a lethal drug. A death penalty expert said it was an unprecedented failure, and Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the remaining execution for the rest of the year.
Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and taken by ambulance from the prison, her attorneys said. She was being treated at a hospital, but they said they hadn't been told about her condition.
She had been scheduled for execution at 10 a.m. Wednesday for the killing she committed at age 18 and would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. An appeals court stopped the lethal injection just an hour before it was to start and hours later the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that stay.
Officials gave Pike two doses of pentobarbital, her attorneys said in court filings late Wednesday.
Gov. Bill Lee said in a statement that he has ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred" and that the remaining scheduled execution will not take place this year.
"Carrying out a lawfully imposed sentence is among the State's most serious responsibilities, and the people of Tennessee expect it to be done in a manner that is not only legal and constitutional, but is effective," he said.
The Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement that they "followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General's Office."
The state's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes to be administered "if the inmate is not deceased" after the first set. It does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.
Robin M. Maher, executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said what Pike experienced is "singular and unparalleled."
Seven other people have survived medical problems due to an execution team's failure to access a vein to administer lethal injection drugs, but no one has stayed alive after receiving the drugs used in such executions, she said.
Kathleen Walter prays in the area reserved for people opposed to the death penalty outside Riverbend Maximum Security Institution before the planned execution of Christa Pike, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. George Walker IV/AP hide caption
Media witnesses observing from a separate room said officials raised curtains to the execution chamber at 7:27 p.m., showing Pike strapped to a gurney.
"I'm going to leave this world the way I spent most of my life and that is in love," she said in her "last" words. She described herself as at peace.
But Pike remained awake and at one point raised her head and asked prison officials if her arm was supposed to feel that way. It was not clear what she was referencing.
By 8:26 p.m., execution witnesses reported that the second dose of pentobarbital had been administered.
Pike continued to be heard snoring behind the closed curtain until the microphone was cut off at 8:53 p.m. At that time there was an announcement to escort media witnesses out of the area.
Lawyers for Pike filed an emergency motion late Wednesday to the Tennessee Supreme Court seeking to immediately halt and stay the execution, saying she was in "unnecessary agony" and it was violating her right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment. They also filed motions in the Sixth Circuit court and a district court.
It was the second time this year that Tennessee has been unable to carry out an execution: In May state officials called off the lethal injection of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and killing three people in 1994, after executioners tried and failed for over an hour to place an IV to administer pentobarbital.
Pike and her boyfriend were convicted of the fatal stabbing and beating in 1995 of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, their classmate at a job training facility in Knoxville. The case garnered widespread attention in part because of a pentagram that was carved on Slemmer's body and other elements of the crime stoked fears of Satan worship during the "satanic panic" of the 1980s and 1990s.
Pike was initially scheduled to be put to death in the morning, and witnesses had gathered at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville when the 6th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals voted 2-1 to issue a stay. That court said a delay was needed to consider whether Pike's allegations of childhood sexual abuse were fully considered at her sentencing.
The attorney general's office appealed to the Supreme Court, saying that halting the execution at the last moment traumatized Slemmer's family and rewarded "abusive delay tactics" by Pike's attorneys.
Later in the day, the high court cleared the way for the execution to proceed. The conservative majority did not explain their order, while the three liberal members signed a dissent that said Pike's claims deserved a closer look.
Pike did not deny committing the killing, but her supporters argued that the state should consider her age at the time, her mental illness and her allegations of severe sexual abuse.
May Martinez, left, mother of murder victim Colleen Slemmer, walks out of Riverbend Maximum Security Institution during a stay of the planned execution of Christa Pike, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, in Nashville, Tenn. George Walker IV/AP hide caption
As the execution date drew near, debate renewed over the death penalty for young offenders.
Assistant Federal Defender Stephen Ferrell said Pike's death sentence is an outlier because other 18-year-olds in Tennessee have had such sentences vacated.
After the killing, Pike was diagnosed with bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder. In her clemency petition, she said she only wanted to fight Slemmer but killed her in a frenzied attack when she couldn't "put the brakes on."
"I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid. It took me numerous years to even realize the gravity of what I'd done," Pike said in a statement.
Slemmer's mother had traveled to Nashville in the hopes of witnessing the execution of her daughter's killer. She told The Associated Press on Saturday that she had waited decades to see Pike's sentence carried out.
"Every time I think about it, I think about Colleen feeling that pain and trying to get up and run," May Martinez told The Associated Press in a telephone interview on Saturday.
Martinez could not be immediately reached by telephone for comment after the execution was halted.
The killing rocked the city of Knoxville. Prosecutors said Pike, fearing Slemmer was trying to steal her boyfriend, lured her to a wooded area on Jan. 12, 1995. Pike cut Slemmer with a box cutter and beat her with a large chunk of asphalt. Shipp, Pike's boyfriend, has admitted that he was the one who carved a pentagram, a star-shaped symbol associated with Satan, into her body.
Shipp was 17 when the crime happened and received a sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole. Pike was the only one sentenced to death.
Since the Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty in 1976, 18 women have been put to death, representing about 1% of all executions, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.
Pike would have been the 30th person executed in the U.S. this year after Florida carried out an execution on Tuesday.
Tennessee announced in 2024 that it was switching from a three-drug series for lethal injections to the single drug pentobarbital. That came more than two years after the state abruptly halted the execution of Oscar Smith and acknowledged that it had failed to ensure its lethal injection drugs were tested properly.

articles.title_orig: Ben Affleck Used AI “For Lots of Things” in His New Netflix Movie ‘Animals’
articles.title_zh: Ben Affleck Used AI “For Lots of Things” in His New Netflix Movie ‘Animals’
articles.content_orig:
Ben Affleck used AI “for lots of things” in his upcoming Netflix thriller Animals , he said Wednesday at Bloomberg ‘s 2026 Screentime event. Not that he’s going to tell you which things.
“I used [AI] for lots of things in that movie. I’m a little bit hesitant to point out what they are — or even talk about it — because in my business, we’re trying to foster the illusion of reality, right?” he told Bloomberg reporter Lucas Shaw. “It’s sort of like if you went to a magic show and the magician walked out and said, ‘Just before I start, I want you to know there’s another bunny under here. (And] this guy’s a plant.’ You know, it’s sort of ruined, right? But yes, we did use it, and in fact, I thought it was a good example (of how to use AI ethically) because it’s a very human movie.”
Other humans in the movie include Gillian Anderson, Steven Yuen and Kerry Washington; Animals premieres on Netflix on Oct. 9.
At this point, Affleck and Netflix are deeply in bed together when it comes to AI. Affleck sold his AI company InterPositive to the streamer for nearly $600 million, so he’s much more bullish on the technology than your average Hollywood heavyweight. He’s also far more knowledgable.
But word is getting out and panic is subsiding, he said. Once a filmmaker spends time with AI tools and gain “a sense of control” over it, the technology “moves from this nebulous, abstract, terrifying alien — you know, ‘It’s going to kill us all,’ all this propaganda — and they actually see what it is,” everyone chills out, Affleck said.
“It’s another form of computing… a technological advancement that’s really in keeping with the longstanding series of technological improvements we’ve made in the film and television business,” he continued. Affleck further stated that he doesn’t believe AI will ever provide the ability for a filmmaker to “type [a prompt] in and make a movie that people want to see.”
Also during the conversation, Affleck dispelled the notion that Netflix made him and Matt Damon regularly restate the plot of their movie The Rip . Affleck says he and Damon went on Joe Rogan’s podcast to explain that their experience with the streaming giant “was utterly contrary” to the Damon quote that quickly went viral.
“Somebody went ahead and did a pull quote, and it got picked up once, and it was, ‘Matt Damon says Netflix makes you tell the plot in the first five minutes,'” Affleck recalled. “If you just stop and think about it— I’m in this movie, I’m directing. Even if that were true, do you think I would go on Joe Rogan and be like, ‘They made me put all this obvious shit in my movie’? Like, it doesn’t even make sense.”
To be fair, it was awfully confusing the way Damon said what he said .
“For instance, Netflix — the standard way to make an action movie, that we learned, was you usually have three set pieces. One in the first act, one in the second, one in the third — and the big one with all the explosions and you spend most of your money on that one in the third act. That’s your kind of finale,” Damon said on The Joe Rogan Experience . “Now, [Netflix is] like, ‘Can we get a big one in the first five minutes?’ We want people to stay tuned in. And it wouldn’t be terrible if you reiterated the plot three or four times in the dialogue because people are on their phones while they’re watching.”
“[Netflix] would never do that,” Affleck said tonight. “I don’t know that I’ve never met anyone who’s had a note that idiotic and brazen — and I’ve heard of a lot of idiotic studio notes. Idiotic studio notes long predate Netflix. This is a business with a long history of executives telling you to do the exact wrong thing that’s going to ruin your movie.”

American officials increasingly believe China is unlikely to attack Taiwan before 2028, despite President Xi Jinping ordering his military to be able to seize the island by force by 2027, according to sources familiar with Washington's assessments.
China's military readiness has been hampered by Xi's sweeping anti-corruption purge, while Beijing may also want to see the outcome of Taiwan's 2028 presidential election before deciding its next move, two serving US officials, a former official and another person familiar with the matter said.
But the risk of military action could rise significantly if Taiwan's ruling Democratic Progressive Party wins an unprecedented fourth consecutive presidential term, particularly if President Lai Ching-te is reelected.
"If that happens, I think 2028 becomes pretty sporty," one US official said.
Lai and the DPP champion Taiwan's separate identity, angering Beijing, which considers the self-governed island part of its territory. Taiwan rejects China's sovereignty claims and says its people can decide its future.
The assessment marks a shift from concerns about 2027, when Xi ordered the People's Liberation Army to be capable of taking Taiwan by force. US officials have long viewed the date, which marks the PLA's centenary, as a military readiness target rather than a firm invasion deadline.
Beijing has never publicly acknowledged plans to attack Taiwan in 2027 and continues to say it favors peaceful "reunification," while refusing to renounce the use of force.
US intelligence agencies have also previously identified signs of caution. In their annual threat assessment in March, they said Beijing had no fixed timeline for invading Taiwan and continued to prefer taking control of the island without war if possible.
The Pentagon declined to comment. The Chinese Embassy in Washington and Taiwan's representative office did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Washington remains Taipei's primary global benefactor and defense vendor despite lacking official diplomatic relations, though American officials provided varying views regarding how heavily Beijing might weigh the outcome of the 2028 U.S. presidential election when evaluating potential military maneuvers.
Although three sources said Chinese strategists might want to gauge the U.S. political outcome—especially amid waning public enthusiasm in America for overseas military engagements—the primary U.S. official emphasized that Beijing considers both Democratic and Republican parties essentially unified in their firm backing of Taiwan.
While Chinese leadership might prefer a certain outcome in the 2028 American vote, "it doesn't become as decisive a factor in my opinion, as it might have been 15 years ago," the official said.
President Donald Trump has consistently minimized the threat of an imminent Chinese assault on Taiwan under his watch, claiming publicly last year that Xi personally assured him Beijing would abstain from invading while he remained in power.
Trump offered brief remarks on Taiwan after his bilateral meeting with Xi in Washington last week, confirming only that Taiwan came up during their exchange and that Xi fully understood his stance.
Beijing repeatedly describes Taiwan as its paramount political priority and a non-negotiable matter touching upon sovereign integrity.
China has persistently demanded a complete halt to American military aid to Taiwan. Following his May visit to Beijing, Trump suspended approval of an approximate $14 billion arms deal, characterizing the military assistance package as a leverage tool or "negotiating chip."
Decades of American policy have concentrated on bolstering Taiwan's defensive capacity, enabling the island to withstand an initial Chinese offensive until Washington and partner nations can intervene defensively.
Chinese leader Xi has not formally abandoned his directive ordering the People's Liberation Army to possess full operational capability to seize Taiwan by force next year, officials noted.
However, the armed forces failed to meet their target operational benchmarks over the past year because Beijing's extensive anti-corruption sweep disrupted progress, sources explained.
Since assuming power in 2012, Xi has spearheaded an uncompromising campaign targeting corruption and party disloyalty. Millions of bureaucrats across China's state apparatus have faced investigation, resulting in the downfall and removal of numerous high-ranking party leaders, officials, and commanders.
Recently, the People's Liberation Army became a primary focus of this internal purge. A wave of high-level inquiries and dismissals leaves only two active members on the once seven-person Central Military Commission, including Xi, who remains chair.
Chinese military maneuvers last year were visibly smaller in scale and less aggressive than in previous periods, according to the U.S. official. Although drills expanded somewhat this year, the official indicated top Chinese military commanders remained privately dissatisfied with force readiness levels.
The official noted Beijing appears to have extracted critical insights from recent conflicts in Iran and Ukraine, realizing that an invasion requires immediate, overwhelming success to prevent becoming entangled in an exhausting, prolonged war of attrition.
Significant operational hurdles remain unaddressed.
"There are way too many pieces that aren't quite in place yet for what would be the most difficult military operation any military has attempted probably since the Allied invasion of Normandy," the official said.

articles.title_orig: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports to bolster stocks, sources say
articles.title_zh: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports to bolster stocks, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oil prices rose on Thursday, reversing earlier losses, following a report that Chinese refiners have suspended October fuel exports, further squeezing war-constrained energy markets.
International benchmark Brent crude with December expiry was last seen trading 2.2% higher at $100.15 per barrel, having earlier traded 1% lower, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures with November expiry rose 1.5% to $91.74.
Reuters reported that China's state oil major PetroChina canceled a handful of gasoline and jet fuel shipments that were planned for October, citing multiple unnamed sources, as Beijing looks to safeguard domestic supplies. CNBC could not independently verify the report.
Global energy markets have been grappling with supply disruptions from the U.S.-Iran war in the Middle East and Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Oil prices had moved higher earlier in the session as investors parsed a recovery in Middle East crude exports.
UOB in a note Thursday said that crude flows from Middle East were reportedly nearing pre-war levels, but fuel supplies, particularly gasoline, were lagging behind.
Worries over crude supply disruptions have eased following the resumption of oil tanker ​loadings by Saudi Arabia from its Red Sea port of Yanbu after the kingdom restarted operations on its East-West Pipeline.
"The pipeline has done much of the heavy lifting when it came to moving crude out of the Gulf," given that Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz, said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation on Wednesday.
"Analysts say that the pipeline is nowhere near running at full capacity. But the fact that it is open provides some relief and has helped oil prices retreat," Morrison added.
Traders continue to keep a close eye on developments in the Middle East amid concerns that a lasting resolution to the Iran conflict may be delayed, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordering the Iranian delegation visiting America to leave as the UN General Assembly was over, according to MS Now.
U.S. and Iranian officials had reportedly held separate indirect talks with mediators on Monday, while in New York for the UNGA.

articles.title_zh: Tesla upgrades China Model 3 with 16-inch screen and V2L, US left out
articles.content_orig:
Tesla China is upgrading every Model 3 it sells with a larger 16-inch touchscreen and a new light gray interior option, and it’s turning on up to 2.2 kW of AC power export across its entire Model 3 and Model Y lineup in the country.
The US Model 3 gets none of it. Tesla’s American Model 3 still has a 15.4-inch display, and it’s shut out of the vehicle-to-load feature Tesla launched stateside in August.
Tesla announced the changes on October 1 with a set of four marketing posters on its official Chinese channels.
The main hardware change is the center display. Every current Model 3 trim in China now gets a 16-inch touchscreen, up from 15.4 inches. Tesla says it has a higher resolution and a higher refresh rate, but it didn’t give actual numbers for either.
The second change is cosmetic. Chinese buyers can now option a light gray “premium interior,” which Tesla pairs with a black fabric headliner. That’s the same move Tesla made on the US Model Y Premium back in January, when it added a black headliner and the 16-inch screen to the 2026 Model Y .
Then there’s power export. Every Model 3 and Model Y currently on sale in China can now push out up to 2,200 W of AC power. Tesla’s example is a camping setup running a 600 W rice cooker, a 1 kW hot pot, and a 600 W electric kettle at the same time.
Owners need to buy Tesla’s AC power-export adapter to use it. The only exception is the three-row Model Y L, which doesn’t need the adapter.
The upgrades came bundled with a new round of incentives. Model 3 orders placed by October 31 get 5,000 yuan (~$740) off the final payment.
Tesla is stacking that with 5-year 0% financing (79,900 yuan down, from about 2,377 yuan per month), an 8,000 yuan insurance subsidy on the RWD, Long Range RWD, and Long Range AWD, an 8,000 yuan paint credit, and a choice of three charging perks.
After all that, Tesla advertises the Model 3 from 222,500 yuan (~$33,000). But the list price didn’t move. The base RWD is still 235,500 yuan, so the headline price only works once you count both the final-payment discount and the insurance subsidy.
Even after discounts, it’s well above BYD’s new Formula S, which starts at 189,900 yuan for the RWD sedan .
We only at least try to pretend to compete where we feel the pressure of competition. The others can live with the scrubs.
We are not a car company, we are a company promising business models but having none.
The competition is fierce in China and Tesla is launching new features and incentives there first.
In the US, the Model 3 starts at $36,990, and Tesla’s own spec page still lists a 15.4-inch center touchscreen.
V2L is the bigger gap. When Tesla brought vehicle-to-load to the US in August , it limited it to the Model Y Premium, Model Y Performance, and Cybertruck, at 2.4 kW through an $80 adapter for the Gen 3 Mobile Connector. The entire US Model 3 lineup was left out. In China, every Model 3 gets it.

articles.title_orig: Japan Raises Residency Fees 2,000 Percent Amid ‘Anxiety’ Over Foreigners
articles.title_zh: Japan Raises Residency Fees 2,000 Percent Amid ‘Anxiety’ Over Foreigners
articles.content_orig:
Japan has raised fees for foreigners seeking permanent residency in the country by 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955).
Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements.
Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours.
The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim to manage its rapidly growing foreign population.
In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years. Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations".
Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage.
Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year. This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change.
Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year.
In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows.
"To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote.
Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay.
From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.
Applicants who face financial hardship or are designated as refugees would be granted discounts.
Aspiring permanent residents must now also earn a stable income at or above the Japanese average. Latest data released in July puts average household income at 5.75 million yen as of 2024.
Micaiah Stevens, who has been living and working in Tokyo for 10 years, was not able to compile the necessary documentation to submit his application for permanent residency before the price hike.
The 37-year-old still plans to apply, but questions the new measures aimed at foreign residents.
"My immediate reaction was that foreigners were being treated a bit too conveniently. We're being asked to make more than the average Japanese person, pay a significantly higher fee, just to be able to work in Japan and provide taxes," he tells the BBC.
"There's already a significant language and cultural barrier that prevents some talent from coming over. This just doesn't strike me as a plan that was thought out to the long term."
From April next year, permanent residency applicants will face even tighter requirements, including basic Japanese language proficiency. This has led to a surge in enrollments at Japanese language schools as well as people signing up to take the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test, local media reported.
Applicants' expected pension benefits must also be equivalent to that of someone who has enrolled into the employee pension system for 30 years, although the value of one's financial assets can be considered if their expected pension benefits fall short.

Jim Carrey recently married his girlfriend Min Ah in a private ceremony.
The couple has been spotted together as far back as 2022, but details of their relationship remain scarce.
Carrey has been married twice, shares one child with ex Melissa Womer, and has dated Linda Ronstadt, Renée Zellweger, January Jones, and Jenny McCarthy.
Congratulations are in order for Jim Carrey , who has married Min Ah.
The Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind star, 64, and his girlfriend recently tied the knot, his rep confirmed to Entertainment Weekly . TMZ reports that they swapped vows in a small, private ceremony in Los Angeles.
EW has reached out to reps for Carrey.
He and Ah made their official debut as a couple on Feb. 26 at the César Awards in Paris, where he was also alongside his adult daughter, Jane, and her teenage son, Jackson.
When the Ace Ventura: Pet Detective star received an honorary award, he made sure to shout out Ah during the speech he gave in French, per PEOPLE .
"Thank you to my wonderful family, my daughter Jane, and my grandson Jackson. I love you now and forever," the actor said through translation. "Thank you to my sublime companion, Min Ah," he said in French, as his daughter, grandson, and girlfriend received ovations from the crowd. "I love you, Min Ah. And finally, thank you to the funniest man I have ever known: my father, Percy Joseph Carrey who taught me the value of love, generosity, and laughter."
Carrey and Ah were first photographed together in 2022.
The actor has been married twice before. He and Melissa Womer, with whom he shares Jane, were married from 1987 to 1995. In 1996, Carrey married Dumb and Dumber costar Lauren Holly, but they split the following year.
Carrey has also had relationships with famous women including Jenny McCarthy, Renée Zellweger, Linda Ronstadt, and January Jones.
Jim Carrey and Min Ah with Jane Erin Carrey and Jackson Riley Credit: Francois Durand/Getty
The union with Ah was consummated despite Carrey's insistence that he wouldn't walk down the aisle again.
He said it in a March 2008 interview with Britain's Weekend Magazine : "I'm happy with Jenny," Carrey said of McCarthy. "Although I probably won't get married again. If you've done it twice, you really should stop doing it."
He confirmed his stance on Howard Stern's SiriusXM radio show in 2014.
"I just don't see it as necessary, at this point," Carrey said. "I can't say that I know how I would feel if I meet somebody that knocks my head off. I mean, I can't make hard, fast rules about the future. But I wouldn't voluntarily go that way."
Looks like his "sublime companion" changed his mind.

articles.title_zh: Steelers trade Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys
articles.content_orig:
Last year, once the Cowboys realized that linebacker Micah Parsons wasn’t going to play without a new contract, Dallas traded him.
This year, the Steelers apparently have realized that cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wouldn’t be playing without a new contract. And so they’re trading him.
Per multiple reports, the Steelers are sending Porter to the Cowboys.
The full terms have yet to emerge. The separate question will be whether the Cowboys will give Porter the contract he couldn’t get in Pittsburgh.
Dallas could decide to ride it out in 2026, with Porter making $3.924 million. Then, they could apply the franchise tag in 2027.
It’s hard to imagine the Cowboys tradining for a player who apparently doesn’t intend to play until he gets a new deal.
The common link between Porter, a second-round pick in 2023, and Parsons is that both are represented by David Mulugheta of Athletes First. Mulugheta also represents receiver George Pickens, who was traded by the Steelers to the Cowboys in May 2025.
The Cowboys haven’t given Pickens a new deal. For 2026, they tagged him. For receivers, the franchise tender is well below market value. It is for cornerbacks, too.
Much will be revealed in the coming hours. For now, the most important point is that the impasse between the Steelers and Porter has ended with Porter being sent to a new team.

articles.title_orig: Yankees send Red Sox home again, move on to face Rays in ALDS
articles.title_zh: Yankees send Red Sox home again, move on to face Rays in ALDS
articles.content_orig:
Playing nine innings while wondering why not-ready-for-prime-time Chad Tracy thought it was a good idea to yank his two best starting pitchers after 4⅔ innings each …
1. This lousy new wait ‘til next year that the Red Sox stuck us with Tuesday night? It feels an awful lot like last year’s season sayonara . Maybe even a little worse.
In last year’s wild-card round duel with the Yankees, at least the Sox won a game, with ace Garrett Crochet delivering a gem in Game 1 . The 2025 Yankees won the next two in the silly best-of-three format, with Cam Schlittler and friends shutting out the Sox in a suspense-free Game 3 .
This year? The Sox went down wheezing. Schlittler, the heavy favorite for the AL Cy Young award, rendered them hopeless in a 9-0 Game 1 win Tuesday. The Yankees ended the Red Sox’ season with a 9-2 pummeling Wednesday night , and you don’t need a calculator to tally up a run differential between these teams. (Yankees, plus-16.)
The better team probably won last year. This year? There is no doubt. The Red Sox were outmanaged, outclassed, and as usual since the start of September, outhit . It stinks to lose to the Yankees once, and it double-stinks to lose to them in back-to-back years.
2. But if we’re being honest with ourselves, there is justice with this outcome. Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow did not build a good enough offense; we suspected it pretty much since their magical, improbable 32-5 stretch from late June through early August curved back to reality.
And wouldn’t you know it, their bats snoozed through another abrupt postseason stay. Yes, the Red Sox were stung by injuries . But deep retrospection is not required to recognize that they never quite had enough offense.
3. We have all winter to deconstruct this most peculiar, uneven season, but this we can declare now. Breslow must get at least one high-end bat, and preferably two, presuming the possibility of a lockout doesn’t halt team-building long before the games begin.
Some marginal players had wonderful stretches for the Red Sox this season, but earth eventually called them back from the stratosphere.
For the last month, I’ve been wondering what this team would have looked like if Breslow had retained Alex Bregman (28 homers, .819 OPS for the Cubs) and signed Pete Alonso (an American League-leading 43 homers and 113 RBIs for the Orioles).
4. I don’t understand any reaction to Roman Anthony’s latest injury other than disappointment for him and deep concern that serious injuries are going to prevent him from becoming the superstar his talent suggests he can be.
Anthony was good for 3.3 wins above replacement in just 75 games upon coming up to the majors last June as a 21-year-old. An oblique injury — rotten to have as a hitter, as James Wood and Drake Baldwin, among others, discovered this season — ended his season abruptly.
Just more than six months ago, he proved he belonged on stage with the best players on the planet during the World Baseball Classic . Hard to believe that was this calendar year.
5. Not much has gone right since the WBC, to put it mildly, and the vast majority of that is not his fault. He started slowly, which happens. A complicated hand/finger injury cost him four months this season, and another ended his season Tuesday night.
Yet in 126 career regular-season games, he has an .803 OPS and 126 OPS+ at 22 years old. It stinks that a player of such obvious promise keeps suffering legitimate injuries.
6. Oh, and it’s borderline pathetic that a portion of the fan base — no doubt including a number of hot takers who think they should get a weekday gig at WEEI whenever the next lineup shakeup comes — have taken to calling Anthony soft or some other synonym.
It’s not as if he’s sitting out with a sprained hair follicle or something. This is an alarming, recurring injury that makes you wonder if his immense promise will be fulfilled.
7. Turns out that Garrett Crochet , who hadn’t pitched in a big league game since April 25 due to shoulder inflammation and then a lat strain, wasn’t quite ready to get back on a big-league mound, let alone under win-or-go-home circumstances.
Crochet allowed four earned runs without recording an out in the sixth inning, though he should have had one — he struck out Spencer Jones, but a wild strike three evaded Adley Rutschman and allowed Jones to reach first base. A tip of the cap to Crochet, however, for giving it a shot.
8. Payton Tolle and Sonny Gray each allowed a single run in 4⅔ innings during their starts. Those single runs each gave the Yankees a 1-0 lead that felt more like 5-0. They both did their jobs, and as noted above, their manager should have allowed them to do it a little longer. Tolle was the best thing about this season, wasn’t he?
9. The Red Sox have not played a postseason game at Fenway Park since a 9-1 loss to the Astros in Game 5 of the 2021 ALCS . The Red Sox lineup that night included Kyle Schwarber, Rafael Devers, Xander Bogaerts, and J.D. Martinez. Five years later, the Sox could have used those guys in the lineup in this series. Yep, even Martinez.

Sean ' Diddy ' Combs is reportedly being sent back to solitary confinement at FCI Fort Dix prison in New Jersey , following claims about his VIP treatment inside .
The disgraced hip-hop mogul, 56, is returning to solitary in response to a recent NBC News report about the alleged special treatment he's been receiving from inmates willing to do his bidding – from cooking, cleaning to even offering massages.
Sources told TMZ it is the standard procedure for an inmate while prison officials conduct an investigation.
The rapper was previously put in solitary confinement back in July after getting into a fight with another inmate.

Diddy's representative Juda S Engelmayer told the Daily Mail about the recent reports: 'There is no way we can independently verify those rumors.'

Four men who spent time in Diddy's unit opened up to the publication about his allegedly luxurious lifestyle – revealing how the music mogul has been living it up during his years-long prison sentence.

Photos obtained by the publication show the meals prepared by inmates specifically for him and others  – pizza and a plate of meat with rice.
'This is not some normal s*** you see in jail. This is some rich s***,' according to one of the men.
In response to the article, Engelmayer told The Daily Mail: 'The continued scrutiny of every mundane detail of Sean Combs's life in prison has reached the point where the media characterizes ordinary prison life as news.'

articles.content_orig:
ST. PETERSBURG -- The Yankees and Rays have shared the field for plenty of memorable moments, tightly contested games and deeply rooted disagreements over the years. They are natural rivals in the American League East, pitting New York’s history and high-payroll dominance against Tampa Bay’s ingenuity and lower-budget success.
They’ve shared the top spot in the standings, too. Since Tampa Bay’s worst-to-first turnaround in 2008, the Rays have won the division five times and the Yankees have won it six times.
But they’ve never shared the postseason spotlight quite like they will in this American League Division Series.
Believe it or not, the Rays and Yankees have only met in the playoffs once before. That matchup came in the 2020 ALDS, the unforgettable back-and-forth affair capped by Mike Brosseau’s game-winning home run off Aroldis Chapman, a distillation of the clubs’ “David vs. Goliath” narrative. But that series took place in San Diego’s Petco Park, a neutral site, during the pandemic.
Now, these two AL powers will square off in their home ballparks with a chance to advance to the AL Championship Series. The series begins Saturday night at Tropicana Field, where the Rays went 55-26 this season in their return to their home dome. It will move to Yankee Stadium, where the Yankees went 46-34 but couldn’t stop their rival from celebrating a division title on their field.
What will the latest installment of this rivalry bring? We’ll soon find out.
"They play fundamental baseball, and they're a team that's going to grind out a game with you," said Yankees captain Aaron Judge. "Those are the type of opponents you look forward to. It's going to be a grind the next five games, but I think the boys are excited and ready to go."
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 1 of the Yankees-Rays Division Series is set for 6:30 p.m. ET on Saturday at Tropicana Field. The game will be broadcast on TBS, truTV and HBO Max.
The ALDS will be available in Spanish on UniMas, while Univision’s TUDN Radio will provide Spanish language audio coverage. ESPN Radio will provide live national coverage of all 2026 MLB Postseason games.
Postseason Guide • Final bracket • Wild Card Series matchups • How to watch Wild Card Series on NBC, Peacock • Postseason schedule
Who are the starting pitchers?
Yankees: Gerrit Cole , RHP or Carlos Rodón , LHP Key stats : Cole 1-1, 2.50 ERA in 3 GS vs. Tampa Bay in 2026; Rodón 1-0, 0.00 ERA in 1 GS vs. Tampa Bay in 2026
The Yankees have not yet announced their starting pitcher for Game 1, but pitching coach Matt Blake said it will either be Cole or Rodón. Cam Schlittler is in line to pitch Game 2 and, if necessary, Game 5.
Had the AL Wild Card Series advanced to Game 3, Cole was in line to start; Rodón was in the bullpen, awaiting a starting assignment in Game 1. That could still go to the lefty, who was sharper down the stretch. Rodón was 3-0 with a 1.42 ERA in four September starts, while Cole was 3-2 with a 5.08 ERA in five September starts, struggling at times to keep the ball in the yard.
“Carlos and I, we’re all just taking the ball,” Cole said. “We’re all just a little bit unique, I think, in the way we do it. I’m stoked. I’m really stoked about it, to be honest. I couldn’t have done it without a lot of the people that are pouring into it behind the scenes. It just means a little bit more to me.”
Rays: Drew Rasmussen , RHP Key stats : 5-2 with a 1.81 ERA and 0.86 WHIP vs. Yankees in regular season (11 games, 10 starts)
Rasmussen is “the standard” for Rays pitchers, one of the best arms in franchise history and undoubtedly the starter Tampa Bay wants on the mound to begin a short series. The last time he pitched in the regular season was at Yankee Stadium, where he carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning and struck out 11 batters in the Rays’ division-clinching victory over the Yankees.
That kind of success against the Yankees was nothing new for Rasmussen, who -- for reasons even he doesn’t fully comprehend -- has had their number over the years. Granted, the 31-year-old right-hander pitches well against pretty much everyone he faces. He led all AL pitchers in WHIP and strikeout-to-walk ratio, finished second in wins and ranked fourth with a 2.67 ERA this season.
What might the starting lineups look like?
Yankees : Judge's presence loomed large during the regular season, when the Yankees averaged 5.12 runs per game with the captain in the lineup and just 4.22 without him. But that flipped in the Wild Card Series against Boston, when they scored 18 runs in the two-game sweep. They’ll look to keep that level of production going, with or without Judge.
1. Ben Rice , DH 2. Cody Bellinger , LF 3. Luis García Jr. , 2B 4. Spencer Jones , RF 5. George Lombard Jr. , SS 6. Jazz Chisholm Jr. , 2B 7. Trent Grisham , CF 8. Austin Wells , C 9. Ryan McMahon , 3B
Rays: The Rays’ lineup could change considerably depending on who the Yankees elect to start Game 1. If it’s a right-hander like Cole, it could look a lot like this. If it’s a lefty like Rodón, there will be significant changes, with Ryan Vilade most likely getting the nod in right field, Jonny DeLuca in center, Ben Williamson at second base and Nick Fortes an option behind the plate. Of course, all eyes will be on the “Big Three” atop the order no matter how the Rays line up behind them.
1. Yandy Díaz , DH 2. Jonathan Aranda , 1B 3. Junior Caminero , 3B 4. Liam Hicks , C 5. Chandler Simpson , LF 6. Victor Mesa Jr. , RF 7. Cedric Mullins , CF 8. Richie Palacios , 2B 9. Taylor Walls , SS
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Yankees: After carrying 10 pitchers for the Wild Card Series, the Yankees figure to have a few extra arms in the bullpen, potentially shifting back to a more conventional 12-pitcher staff. One of their toughest calls was between Tim Hill and Ryan Yarbrough; Hill could be back on for this round. Ryan Weathers touched 96 mph as he recovers from a left flexor strain and should be in play for the ALDS. David Bednar, Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick should all be leaned upon for high-leverage outs.
Rays: We won’t know for sure until the Rays set their roster and reveal their rotation plans beyond Game 1. But it’s probably easiest to start at the back end, where All-Star closer Bryan Baker was a rock in the ninth inning (and occasionally in the eighth, if needed). They have a solid setup crew in front of Baker in Tyler Wells, assuming he returns from a forearm issue , and the righty-lefty duo of Kevin Kelly and Cam Booser. Those four seem likely to get the biggest outs of the game, but it’s possible manager Kevin Cash could turn to one of his other starters -- perhaps a lefty like Ian Seymour, who performed well against the Yankees this season -- to build a bridge from Rasmussen to the high-leverage arms.
Yankees: Judge took live at-bats on Wednesday in Bridgewater, N.J., and may do so again on Thursday before traveling with the team to Tropicana Field, where Friday’s workout promises to be watched closely. As of Wednesday, Judge still had yet to run the bases as he recovers from a right calf strain , though he has been performing outfield running. Weathers is close to returning from his left flexor strain and is very much in the bullpen mix.

Same goes for left-hander Shane McClanahan , whose status is unclear except that he will not pitch in this series. articles.content_orig:
Democratic governor sharply critical of Donald Trump for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations
Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting California workers from the threats of artificial intelligence , including potential job losses and workplace surveillance.
The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone.
The Democratic governor also signed an executive order to require state agencies to continue to refer to the technology as “artificial intelligence” instead of the term “super intelligence” as Donald Trump recently ordered US diplomats to use.
“AI should expand opportunity – not come at the expense of workers and families,” Newsom said in a statement. “As this technology reshapes the workplace, California is putting people at the center.”
He sharply criticized Trump at an hour-long event with reporters Wednesday for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations at a time when industry leaders are warning about the technology’s risks. Trump said Tuesday that top tech leaders signed a voluntary accord to “self-police” AI development.
The governor signed a law this month requiring operators of AI chatbots to perform risk assessments before rolling them out and an executive order requiring the state to consult with experts to further improve oversight over the industry.
“We have to do a lot more in the absence of federal leadership,” Newsom said, leaving the door open for the possibility of calling lawmakers back for a special session to further tackle the issue.
The news conference came on Newsom’s last day to sign or veto bills before he terms out in January. He started the event by signing a law creating a tax credit program aimed at helping local news organizations – including newspapers, digital outlets and TV stations – hire and retain journalists. Newsom criticized what he called Trump’s assault on a free press, pointing to the president’s barring of news organizations from the White House.
Newsom also spoke about the upcoming midterms, which will decide control of Congress. He involved himself early in that fight by leading Democrats last year in a redistricting battle to improve their chances of winning more House seats. He’s said repeatedly that the stakes are high if his party doesn’t succeed in November.
“There will not be a free and fair election in 2028 unless we take back the House of Representatives,” he said Wednesday.
Asked if he had set a deadline for himself to decide to run for president in 2028, Newsom hedged, saying: “That moment will arrive when it arrives.”
Former Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris, who, like Newsom, hails from the San Francisco Bay Area, has also said she’s considering running for the job in 2028. Newsom told CNN recently that he would not run for president if she entered the race. He said the two have not spoken since that interview aired.
Newsom weighed in on a proposal to temporarily raise taxes on billionaires that will be on the ballot in November, which he’s consistently opposed. He said he respects supporters of the measure, including Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, who are committed to addressing income inequality in the country.
“He’s spot on about the balance between the rich and the poor,” Newsom said. “On this issue, we fundamentally disagree.”
Newsom’s remarks came hours before a gubernatorial debate between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton.
“You’re going to ask me, ‘Are you going to watch the debate?’” he said. “No.”

articles.title_orig: In photos: China's Xi hardens Taiwan warning as country celebrates week-long National Day holiday
articles.title_zh: In photos: China's Xi hardens Taiwan warning as country celebrates week-long National Day holiday
articles.content_orig:
China began its seven-day National Day holiday on Thursday after President Xi Jinping used his annual opening speech to sharpen Beijing's message on Taiwan.
Speaking at the Great Hall of the People on Wednesday, on the eve of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, Xi said Beijing must " resolutely crack down on 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces, oppose interference from external forces" and "advance the great cause of national reunification."
The language is harder than in Xi's speech last year, when he said Beijing "firmly opposes" independence activities .
The shift comes days after Xi's state visit to Washington, where he urged President Donald Trump to outright "oppose" Taiwan independence, and to limit Washington's support for the self-ruled island that Beijing claims its own. That wording would be stronger than the longstanding U.S. position of not supporting Taiwan independence.
"It has been speculated for more than a year that Xi would do this, but it was the first time we saw him do it," said Allan von Mehren, China economist at Danske Bank.
The Trump administration paused a $14 billion Taiwan arms package in May and has struck a less supportive tone toward the island over the past year.
State leaders, including Xi, presented flower baskets at the Monument to the People's Heroes in Tiananmen Square on Wednesday, the country's Martyrs' Day, a day before National Day. Xi walked around the monument in tribute to fallen national heroes, according to photos published by state media .
Crowds in Beijing gathered on Thursday morning to watch the People's Liberation Army honor guard escort the national flag to Tian'anmen Square, with a military band playing the national anthem and thousands of doves released into the sky.
Travelers and city workers are heading out for the holiday, which runs from Thursday through next Wednesday. Workers often stretch the break to 13 days, by taking leave from Monday to Wednesday, spanning the Mid-Autumn Festival on Friday.
China's Ministry of Transport projects about 2.13 billion trips over the holiday week, or roughly 300 million a day.
Daily border crossings are forecast to average about 2.16 million. Bookings for domestic flights over 2,000 kilometers are up about 14%, and international ticket bookings are up 22.5% from a year earlier, according to official figures .
Golden Week is typically a gauge of domestic consumption, but years of subdued consumer demand mean heavy travel may not translate into bigger spending. Trip volumes and revenue rose during last year's holiday but remained around 3% lower than in 2019 before the pandemic, according to Goldman Sachs.
The authorities in Hong Kong expect 7.4 million passenger trips in and out of the city over the upcoming week, and Macau anticipates more than 5 million trips during the holiday.
At a celebration event in Hong Kong on Tuesday, Chief Executive John Lee said the city's first five-year plan would help it "share the rhythm of China's growth."

articles.title_orig: Trump’s AI chatbot turns on its master
articles.title_zh: Trump’s AI chatbot turns on its master
articles.content_orig:
The famously fact-averse president rolled out a new AI tool – but its answers don’t conform to his version of reality
Donald Trump , in a development that could almost be from a Greek tragedy, appears to have invented something that is willing to do what no one in his orbit will: tell him the truth.
The president launched America.gov on Tuesday, an AI platform which the White House says will make it easier for Americans to interact with the federal government and eventually complete services like renewing passports and enrolling in Medicare.
At the heart of the website is a chatbot. You plug in questions. It gives you answers.
Unfortunately for Trump, America.gov – which, according to the executive order he signed, is a place where Americans can “receive accurate answers” to all sorts of questions – is providing the kind of answers that he will not want to hear. It stands ready to debunk his false claims on all sorts of things, including election fraud, inflation and the impact of wind turbines on whales.
I would really recommend testing it out, as I did on Tuesday. I started off by asking Trump’s flagship product: Who won the 2020 election? Trump, famously and wrongly, argues that he did.
America.gov does not have time for such claims. “Joseph R Biden Jr won the 2020 US presidential election,” the bot said, before listing the number of electoral college votes Biden won by.
Next up I tried some of Trump’s more recent claims. This week the president said people were “twice as wealthy as [they] were a short time ago”. Does America.gov agree?
“No. Federal Reserve data do not show American household wealth doubling since January 20, 2025,” it said. “The Fed’s Economic Well-Being of US Households in 2025 found 73% of adults ‘doing okay’ or ‘living comfortably’ – unchanged from recent years, not a doubling of typical household finances.”
Pretty definitive. What about Trump’s ( already debunked ) claim that the US experienced the “worst inflation ever” under Biden? Once again, America.gov disagreed with its creator.
“No. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Price Index data do not show that January 20, 2021–January 20, 2025 was the worst inflation ever in US history.”
There are plenty more examples. Trump’s bot denied his claim, made in a recent speech to the United Nations, that the US and Venezuela have 60% of the world’s oil . It said there was no widespread voter fraud in the 2020 election, in contrast to Trump’s repeated, untrue claims. The bot refuted Trump’s assertion, made as he launched America.gov on Tuesday, that no president other than him had refused to take a government salary.
It was also happy to weigh in on matters which might seem trivial, but are close to Trump’s heart. The attendance at his 2017 inauguration, for example. At the time Trump’s team said he had drawn “the largest audience ever to witness an inauguration, period, both in person and around the globe”.
after newsletter promotion
America.gov said: “Official sources do not support that [2017] had the largest in-person crowd of any US inauguration … The Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies lists Barack Obama’s January 20, 2009 ceremony as having the largest attendance of any presidential inauguration in US history and the largest attendance of any event in Washington, DC history.”
Finally, what about Trump’s claim – made during one of his many rants against wind power – that turbines drive whales “loco”?
“No,” America.gov said. “US federal science agencies do not find that wind turbines (‘windmills’) drive whales ‘loco’.” It added, just to be completely clear, that windmills are not “driving whales insane”.
So who do you believe? A president who, according to the Washington Post, made 30,573 false or misleading claims in his first term? Or his AI platform, which draws upon 29,000 websites to formulate its answers?
Americans encouraged to use what Trump himself has hailed as “the ultimate product” can make up their own mind.

articles.content_orig:
Alphabet plans to launch its homegrown AI chips into orbit on Thursday in a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, a step towards making data centers in space a reality.
The launch is scheduled for 11:15 am PT from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California's Santa Barbara County.
SpaceX has promoted supercomputers in space as the next frontier in artificial intelligence infrastructure, touting "infinite real estate" in orbit as a means of escaping the data center backlash on the ground. During the uncrewed Transporter-18 mission, SpaceX will carry Planet Labs satellites, including a solar-powered prototype equipped with Google's tensor processing units (TPUs).
It marks the first in-orbit test for Alphabet's Project Suncatcher, a "moonshot" initiative Google first revealed in November 2025. The company aims to develop reliable, solar-powered AI computing infrastructure that can operate continuously in space.
In a post announcing the launch plan, Alphabet said Project Suncatcher is a means of "exploring whether space could one day host scalable machine learning infrastructure."
Alphabet is a significant investor in SpaceX, which went public in June in a record IPO, and the businesses are close partners even as their AI divisions compete with one another. Alphabet's stake in SpaceX is currently valued at over $82 billion.
In low Earth orbit, satellites can "access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth," Alphabet said in the post. Eventually, they expect to be able to "link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit."
The Google parent has already tested its TPUs running AI workloads in a facility at the University of California at Davis, but doesn't yet know how its chips will perform in the challenging conditions of low Earth orbit.
SpaceX, led by Elon Musk , has also announced that it plans to build and launch its own orbital data centers. They will be comprised of swarms of satellites the company develops in Redmond, Washington, equipped with graphics processing units and solar arrays it plans to produce with Tesla , Musk's automaker.
Earlier this year, Musk said data centers in space would be the cheapest way to train AI, "and that will be true within two years, maybe three at the latest." SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said at an event in September that the company will deploy "supercompute in space" in 2027.
Industry experts say space-based data centers represent a far-out mission, if they can even become feasible, in part because rocket launches remain capacity-constrained and expensive. Orbital data centers would also require cooling systems and chips that can withstand extreme temperatures, as well as protection from radiation. Clutter and orbital debris could also impede their viability.
The Transporter-18 flight will be the second potentially historic launch in a single day for SpaceX, which is also slated to carry astronauts to the International Space Station from Florida's Space Coast for NASA on Thursday, marking the start of a six-month mission in orbit.

Over the last few years, Chinese Android manufacturers have followed Vivo’s example of launching add-on “teleconverter” lenses for their flagship phones, enabling long-distance photography that the phones on their own could never match. Today, Huawei one-upped everybody with the add-on lens for its Mate 90 Pro Max flagship, which is not only a comically huge zoom lens, but also includes its own image sensor.
The 1-inch-type, 50-megapixel RYYB sensor inside the Ruiying Z10 is bigger than any inside the phone itself, so attaching this lens doesn’t just give you better glass, it’s actually a complete overhaul of the camera capabilities. And while other teleconverters have so far had fixed focal lengths, this is a true zoom lens that covers 24–240mm, with a variable aperture of f/2.0-f/4.5. This is almost a camera in its own right, only using the phone for power, processing, and software.
Impressively, Huawei also appears to have designed the lens to attach directly to compatible phones, instead of needing an intermediary case for a mounting point. The obvious downside to the Z10 is that it’s absolutely enormous, even by teleconverter standards — you’re not going to fit this thing in your pocket. But at 346g, it’s still smaller and more portable than even most mirrorless cameras, and you’ll probably be able to take it into venues where cameras aren’t permitted, like concerts and sports matches. Then there’s the price: at ¥5,999 (around $895), this is more expensive than some flagship phones.
Huawei says the Z10 is compatible with the collector’s edition of the Mate 90 Pro Max and its Mate 90 RS variant, the only two models in the new Mate 90 series with the screw-mount around the camera island. They have impressive cameras in their own right, with an f/1.4-f/4.0, 50-megapixel, variable aperture main camera using a 1.1.28-inch-type sensor; a 200-megapixel 4x periscope telephoto with the same size sensor; and a 40-megapixel ultrawide. The 6.9-inch OLED display can hit 12,000 nits of peak brightness, and it’s powered by a 6,800mAh battery and Huawei’s own Kirin 9050 Pro chip.
